mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a financial crisis period.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which erode consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during a period of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% signals a contraction in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings visibility and increases recession risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a confirmed industrial recession.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the federal funds rate below 1% combined with a concurrent surge in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 3% monthly signals a stagflation risk, which increases uncertainty and risk aversion, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of falling inflation expectations.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of high wage inflation.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) by more than 1% signals a broad-based collapse in residential and consumer demand, which depresses equity valuations and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -1% AND HOUST monthly change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism does not activate during a clear external demand shock.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% per month for three consecutive months, in the absence of a concurrent rise in inflation (CPIAUCSL monthly change ≤ 0.2%), signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that over-tightens credit conditions and suppresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS monthly change > 0.25% for 3 consecutive months AND CPIAUCSL monthly change ≤ 0.2%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a period of rising inflation expectations.
